summary:
Rio Grande do Norte stands under Brazil's national legal framework on gender recognition, anti-discrimination protection and custody placement. The sources reviewed record no state law, state court decision or official policy specific to Rio Grande do Norte on those questions, so the national assessment applies here unchanged.

Lethal violence against trans women is documented in the state in 2026. In the early hours of 4 May 2026 Emanuelle Samira Fernandes Neta, 27, was shot dead inside the rented house where she slept on Rua Vivaldo Dantas in the Dom Jaime Câmara neighbourhood of Mossoró, in the west of the state, after five men broke in. Military police found the body on a routine patrol. One suspect was arrested carrying a pistol and booked for illegal firearms discharge and armed criminal association.

In late February 2026 a transgender woman known as Naomi was found dead inside her own home in Praia da Pipa, in the coastal municipality of Tibau do Sul on the state's southern coast, killed by stab wounds. The Civil Police opened an investigation.

ATTRANSPARÊNCIA/RN, the state's trans-rights association, publicly mourned Emanuelle Samira Fernandes Neta as an artist killed by the transphobia she faced, and called for justice in the Praia da Pipa case.

The state ranking in ANTRA's ninth dossier, covering 2025, records four trans and travesti killings in Rio Grande do Norte against none recorded for the state in 2024, a jump described in the reporting as the sharpest deterioration among the states in that dataset. The figure is a raw count with no population denominator, so it measures recorded incidents rather than per-capita risk; four of the 80 killings recorded nationwide that year fell in the Northeast.

The zero recorded for Rio Grande do Norte in 2024 rests on a dataset its own authors describe as systematically under-counted, because official bodies do not record LGBTQIA+ victims properly. A count of zero in that dataset does not establish an absence of killings, and the state's 2025 and 2026 figures should be read against that undercount.
tangentialFactors:
ANTRA's dossier for 2024 recorded 122 trans and travesti killings across Brazil, 16% below the 145 recorded in 2023 and close to the average of 125 a year for the period 2008 to 2024. Five of the 2024 victims were human-rights defenders and 95.9% of victims were travestis or trans women. The dossier's authors state that official bodies do not record LGBTQIA+ victims properly, so every state-level count, including Rio Grande do Norte's, sits on an undercounted base.

The ninth ANTRA dossier, covering 2025, records 80 killings nationwide, a 34% drop from 2024, and marks an eighteenth consecutive year at the top of the global tally. Ceará and Minas Gerais lead the state ranking with eight each; Rio Grande do Norte and Paraíba appear with four each, and the Northeast as a whole accounts for 38 of the 80. These are raw counts: without population or per-capita figures the ranking reflects reporting capacity and population size as much as danger, and a state with four recorded killings is not thereby shown to be more dangerous than one with fewer residents and fewer records.
localsOnly:
ATTRANSPARÊNCIA/RN is the state-level trans-rights association documented here. It issues public statements on individual killings, mourns victims by name and calls on the Civil Police and prosecutors, and in the sources reviewed it is the principal local channel through which these cases reach the public.

Investigations into killings of trans women in the state run through Rio Grande do Norte's own machinery: the Civil Police opened the Praia da Pipa inquiry in February 2026, and in Mossoró the Military Police processed the scene and the arrest followed within days.

No region-specific provision on identity documents, gender markers, health care, facilities or custody placement was found for Rio Grande do Norte. Residents rely on the national framework, and no state statute or state judicial decision on those questions appears in the sources reviewed.
outOfScopeNotes:
The 2025 state figure is unresolved. The ninth ANTRA dossier ranking records four killings in Rio Grande do Norte for 2025, while figures drawn from the same dossier and reproduced in a February 2026 report state zero registered trans killings in the state for 2025. The sources do not reconcile the two counts, and neither can be verified here.

No population denominator and no general homicide rate for Rio Grande do Norte appear in the sources, so the state's trans-specific killings cannot be set against background violence. The counts are raw totals only.

Two sources reviewed, an encyclopaedia entry on LGBT rights in Brazil and an overview of LGBTQ people in prison read on 28 September 2026, contain no Rio Grande do Norte-specific rule or statistic; the prison provisions they describe apply to Brazil as a whole.

Nothing in this inventory documents Rio Grande do Norte practice on gender-marker issuance by state agencies, access to gender-affirming care within the state, treatment of gender-nonconforming travellers at state facilities, venue refusals, or the housing of trans prisoners in the state prison system. Those questions are unresolved here, not absent.
